title: The Ass, the Ox and the Farmer
text:
At the start of the Thousand and One Nights, before Shahrazad went to the king, her father the vizier tried to warn her with a story.

A rich farmer had been given the gift of understanding animals, on condition that he never revealed what he heard. One evening he overheard his ox complaining to his ass. The ox plowed all day while the ass, who was rarely ridden, rested in a clean stall. The ass gave him advice: tonight, refuse your fodder and lie down as if you were sick, and they will leave you alone.

The ox did exactly that. In the morning the plowman reported that the ox was ill, and the farmer, who had heard everything, smiled and said: then yoke the ass in his place. The ass spent the whole day dragging the plow.

That night, aching and sore, the ass realized his advice had cost him dearly. He told the ox, with great concern, that he had heard the master say that if the ox stayed sick, he would be slaughtered and his hide sold. The frightened ox ate all his fodder, and the next morning he went eagerly to the plow, while the farmer, who had understood every word, laughed out loud.
lesson: Teaching a colleague to dodge work rarely ends well, since someone has to do it, and it may be you. Be careful what shortcuts you recommend to others.
people: An ass, an ox, a farmer who understood animals
date: Medieval; frame story of the collection
source: One Thousand and One Nights, frame story, The Tale of the Ox and the Ass, told by the vizier to Shahrazad
